learning_outcomes.text: Explore, describe, and visualize datasets using descriptive statistics methods.
Model random phenomena using the mathematical language of probability.
Infer properties of the underlying population from sample properties using appropriate inferential statistics tools.
Evaluate, model, develop solutions, and correctly and critically interpret results for quantitative application problems in engineering sciences using the statistical methods learned in the lecture.
Effectively use statistical software to practically implement learned methods and perform reproducible analyses.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Central concepts of statistics, data, data science
Descriptive Statistics: Data visualization methods, measures of central tendency and dispersion, and analysis of bivariate data
Probability Theory: Fundamentals of probability, random variables, and important probability distributions
Inferential Statistics: Estimators, hypothesis tests, and linear regression
Statistical Software Applications: Practical implementation of statistical methods in suitable software packages
Applications in the context of SDGs: Analysis of real datasets on sustainability, environment, health, energy, or social development within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals
assessment_rules: The assessment is a written exam of 90 minutes. Up to 10% of the exam points can be earned during the semester through bonus points from practical exercises.
